# `nish/json-typed`

Decode a JSON object into a class, and encode a class back, with code the compiler writes from the class's fields.

```ts
import {
  JSON_DECODE_DUPLICATE,
  JSON_DECODE_MAP_LIMIT,
  JSON_DECODE_MISSING,
  JSON_DECODE_OK,
  JSON_DECODE_RANGE,
  JSON_DECODE_TYPE,
  JSON_DECODE_UNKNOWN,
  JsonDecoder,
  JsonNumber,
  jsonDecode,
  jsonEncode,
  jsonEncodeBooleanArray,
  jsonEncodeBooleanArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeF64Array,
  jsonEncodeF64ArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeI32Array,
  jsonEncodeI32ArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeI64Array,
  jsonEncodeI64ArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeNumber,
  jsonEncodeStringArray,
  jsonEncodeStringArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeStringOrNull,
  jsonEncodeU32Array,
  jsonEncodeU32ArrayOrNull,
  jsonEncodeU64,
  jsonEncodeU64Array,
  jsonEncodeU64ArrayOrNull,
} from "nish/json-typed";
```

```ts
import { JsonLimits } from "nish/json-tokenizer";
import { JsonWriter } from "nish/json";
import { JsonDecoder, jsonDecode, jsonEncode } from "nish/json-typed";

class Point { x: i32 = 0; y: i32 = 0 }

const d = new JsonDecoder(body, 0, toI32(body.length), new JsonLimits());
const p = new Point();
if (jsonDecode(d, p) === 0) {
  const w = new JsonWriter(out, 0);
  jsonEncode(w, p);              // out[0 .. w.end) is {"x":..,"y":..}
}
```

<scalar-detail title="What is generated, and from what">

`jsonDecode(d, out)` and
`jsonEncode(w, value)` are generic, and the bodies written below are not
what runs natively: the compiler lowers every call in place, in the module
that makes it, to code it writes from the layout of the class the call
binds `T` to (`src/json-typed.ts`, `src/emit-json.ts`). That code is
straight-line calls into the methods of `JsonDecoder` and the functions
here for each field, and into `JsonWriter`'s, so all of the parsing is the
tokenizer's and all of the writing is the writer's. A field may be an
`i32`, `u32`, `i64`, `u64`, `f64` (or `number`), `boolean` or `string`, a
numeric enum (its number), a class decoded the same way, a `JsonNumber`, an
array of any of those, a `Map<string, V>` (a JSON object) whose `V` is any
of these, or a string, class, array or map `| null`; anything else is
refused at the call, naming the field (docs/LANGUAGE.md, "Typed JSON").

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The decoding rules">

A JSON object's keys are the class's field names,
byte for byte, or the keys its options give them, found by the key's length
and then, among three or more names of that length, by one of its bytes:

```text
class Account {
  static readonly json = { rename: { userId: "user_id" }, optional: ["tags"] };
  ...
}
```

</scalar-detail>

The compiler reads that literal; it is not a field. Every field is required
but an optional one, whose missing key sets it to its initializer, a key
may appear once, and a key that names no field is an error unless
`ignoreUnknown` is set, when its value is stepped over. A number must fit its field: an integer field takes
an integer written without a fraction or an exponent and in the field's
range, and `f64` takes any number. `null` is accepted only by a field whose
type is `| null`. Fields are written to `out` as they are read, in the
input's order: a nested object is decoded into the object the field already
holds, an array's elements into the elements it already has (so a reused
object reuses its arrays and objects, and `Arena.used()` stays flat), and a
string field keeps the string it holds when the input's is equal.
A class the decoder has to make — an array element past the array's end, a
`| null` field that holds `null`, or a map's value — is made with `new C()`.
A map is emptied and filled in the input's order, and every map of one
decoding takes at most `maxMapKeys` keys between them.

<scalar-detail title="Which keys were given">

An optional field's missing key and a key given
the field's initializer leave the same value; the `presence` option tells
them apart. It names, for a field, a `boolean` field of the same class that
each decoding sets to whether the input gave that field's key — true for a
key given `null` too:

```ts
class UserPatch {
  static readonly json = { optional: ["name", "email"], presence: { name: "hasName", email: "hasEmail" } };
  name: string = "";
  email: string | null = null;
  hasName: boolean = false;
  hasEmail: boolean = false;
}
```

</scalar-detail>

Any field can be recorded, of any kind and optional or not. A presence
field is off the wire: no key reads it, encoding leaves it out, and no option
renames it, makes it optional or records it. It is set when the object
closes, from the flag the decoder already keeps per field to find a
duplicate or a missing key, so recording costs one store per recorded field
and allocates nothing, and a class that records nothing compiles to the code
it did before. Each object sets its own, so a nested class or an array
element answers for its own keys. A decoding that fails may set some of
them and not others (when the input is not an object, none), so read them
only when `jsonDecode` answered `JSON_DECODE_OK`.

<scalar-detail title="A merge patch (RFC 7396)">

**A merge patch (RFC 7396)** is that option's use: a patch class whose
every field is optional and recorded, decoded and then applied a field at a
time — a recorded key replaces its member, `null` on a `| null` field
removes it, an object field is applied the same way one level down, and an
array is replaced whole. `null` on a field that is not `| null` is
`JSON_DECODE_TYPE`, so a patch that removes what the type cannot lose is
refused before any of it is applied. `examples/merge-patch.ts` is the
recipe in full.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Errors are sticky codes">

**Errors are sticky codes**, as the tokenizer's and the writer's are. The
first error sets `failed` to a negative code — a `JSON_DECODE_*` code here,
or the tokenizer's own `JSON_TOK_ERR_*` code when the text is not JSON or
crosses one of its `JsonLimits` — and `errorAt` to the byte offset of the
token it was found at. Every later call does nothing, and `jsonDecode`
answers `failed`. Nothing an input holds panics. After an error, `out` holds
a value of its type in every field, some of them decoded and some as they
were.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Encoding">

**Encoding** writes the fields in declaration order, each through the
writer method of its type, so the text is what `JSON.stringify` writes for
the same object; the writer's own sticky code reports a full buffer.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Under Node">

**Under Node** the types are erased, so there is no layout to generate the
code from: `jsonDecode` and `jsonEncode` end the program with a panic
naming this, rather than guessing a type from whatever value a field holds
(docs/LANGUAGE.md, "Typed JSON", class C). Everything else here runs there.

</scalar-detail>

Every name here is `json`-prefixed, as `std/json.ts` explains, and every
code is an `i32`, so the module is the same under `--number-mode f64`.

## jsonEncodeU64

A `u64`, as its digits: at most 20 of them, written with `raw` from an
array of this call's own that nothing keeps. A value past 2^63 has no
`i64` to go through the writer's `i64` as, so every `u64` takes this one
loop. Every `u64` here is built with `toU64`, a BigInt under Node.

```ts
function jsonEncodeU64(
  w: JsonWriter,
  v: u64,
): void
```

## JsonDecoder

One decoding: a tokenizer over the input and the sticky error. Make one per
connection and `reset` it per request; nothing it does allocates but the
strings it decodes, the arrays it grows and the objects it makes.

```ts
class JsonDecoder
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JsonDecoder(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, limits: JsonLimits)` |  |
| `errorAt: i32` | The byte offset in the input of the token the error was found at; `-1` until one. |
| `failed: i32` | `JSON_DECODE_OK`, or the first `JSON_DECODE_*` or `JSON_TOK_ERR_*` code. |
| `held: boolean` | Whether the tokenizer's current token is a value nothing has read yet: the first token of an array element, read to see whether the array had ended, or a value `takeNull` found was not `null`. |
| `ignoreUnknown: boolean` | Step over a key that names no field instead of failing with `JSON_DECODE_UNKNOWN`. |
| `mapKeys: i32` | The keys the maps of this decoding have taken so far; `reset` clears it. |
| `maxMapKeys: i32` | The most keys every `Map` field of one decoding may take together, 4,096 unless set; past it, `JSON_DECODE_MAP_LIMIT`. At `0` or below, no map may take a key, so a map's only accepted value is `{}`. |
| `tok: JsonTokenizer` |  |
| `beginArray(): boolean` | The next value opens an array; anything else is `JSON_DECODE_TYPE`. |
| `beginObject(): boolean` | The next value opens an object; anything else is `JSON_DECODE_TYPE`. |
| `boolean(): boolean` |  |
| `booleanArray(xs: boolean[]): boolean[]` |  |
| `booleanArrayOrNull(xs: boolean[] \| null): boolean[] \| null` |  |
| `duplicateField(): void` | The current key names a field the object already gave. |
| `f64(): f64` |  |
| `f64Array(xs: f64[]): f64[]` |  |
| `f64ArrayOrNull(xs: f64[] \| null): f64[] \| null` |  |
| `fail(code: i32, at: i32): void` | Records the first error. |
| `finish(): i32` | After the top-level value: nothing but blanks may follow. Answers `failed`. |
| `i32(): i32` |  |
| `i32Array(xs: i32[]): i32[]` |  |
| `i32ArrayOrNull(xs: i32[] \| null): i32[] \| null` |  |
| `i64(): i64` | Any integer `isInteger` accepts fits an `i64`, so there is no range to check. |
| `i64Array(xs: i64[]): i64[]` |  |
| `i64ArrayOrNull(xs: i64[] \| null): i64[] \| null` |  |
| `integer(lo: i64, hi: i64, bounded: boolean): i64` | The next value as an integer, from `lo` to `hi` when `bounded`, or `0` with an error. Every `i64` it answers is the tokenizer's or made with `toI64`, so that under Node, where an `i64` is a BigInt, what a caller computes with it never mixes a BigInt with a number. |
| `key(): string` | The current key, decoded, as a new string: a `Map` field's key. `""` when the current token is not a key. |
| `keyByte(at: i32): i32` | Byte `at` of the current key when the key has no escape, so that its bytes are the input's, and `-1` otherwise: for a key with an escape, for an `at` outside it, and when the current token is not a key. A `-1` matches no byte of a field's name, and the code written for a class then compares the key with each name of its length through `keyIs`, which decodes the escapes. |
| `keyIs(name: string): boolean` | Whether the current key is `name`. |
| `keyLength(): i32` | The current key's length in bytes once decoded, or `-1` when the current token is not a key: what the code written for a class switches on before it compares a key's bytes with a field's name. |
| `mapRoom(): boolean` | Whether the maps of this decoding may take another key, the current one: whether they have taken fewer than `maxMapKeys` between them, counting it as taken when they may. A key is counted here, before its value is read, so the keys of a map inside another map count before the outer key's value is whole, and the total never passes the limit. `JSON_DECODE_MAP_LIMIT` at the key when they may not. |
| `missingField(): void` | The object just closed without one of the fields. |
| `nextElement(): boolean` | Whether the open array has another element, whose first token is then held; `false` at its end and after any error. |
| `nextField(): boolean` | Reads the next key of the open object, or its end; `false` at the end and after any error. |
| `number(n: JsonNumber): void` | The next value as a `JsonNumber`: its text, copied into `n`'s bytes exactly as the input writes it. Anything but a number is `JSON_DECODE_TYPE`, and `n` keeps the number it held. |
| `reset(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Starts over on `src[off, off + len)`, keeping the limits, `ignoreUnknown` and `maxMapKeys`, and clearing any error and the count of map keys taken. |
| `string(cur: string): string` | The next value as a string: `cur` itself when the input's string is equal to it, which allocates nothing, and a new string otherwise; `cur` with an error. |
| `stringArray(xs: string[]): string[]` |  |
| `stringArrayOrNull(xs: string[] \| null): string[] \| null` |  |
| `take(): i32` | The kind of the next value's first token, or a negative code; the held token first, when there is one. |
| `takeNull(): boolean` | Whether the next value is `null`, read if so; otherwise it is held for the read that follows. |
| `text(): string` | The current key or string as a new string, made by one `String.fromBytes`: straight from the input when it has no escape, and from its unescaped bytes when it has one. `""` when the current token is neither. |
| `u32(): u32` | The bounds are compared and never computed with, so under Node a number beside a BigInt is fine. |
| `u32Array(xs: u32[]): u32[]` |  |
| `u32ArrayOrNull(xs: u32[] \| null): u32[] \| null` |  |
| `u64(): u64` | The next value as a `u64`: an integer written in digits alone, with no sign, fraction or exponent, up to 2^64 - 1, read through the tokenizer's `numberU64`. A negative number, `-0` included, and one past 2^64 - 1 are `JSON_DECODE_RANGE`, as a fraction is; `0` with an error. |
| `u64Array(xs: u64[]): u64[]` |  |
| `u64ArrayOrNull(xs: u64[] \| null): u64[] \| null` |  |
| `unknownField(): void` | The current key names no field: stepped over with its value, or `JSON_DECODE_UNKNOWN`. |
| `wrongType(): void` | `JSON_DECODE_TYPE` at the current token, unless the read that found it failed already. |

## JsonNumber

A JSON number kept as the text it was written in, so that no digit is lost:
an integer wider than a `u64` and a fraction with more digits than an `f64`
holds are decoded and encoded again byte for byte. A field of this class is
read and written as one number, not as an object: `jsonDecode` copies the
number's text into it, and `jsonEncode` writes that text back unchanged.

It reads its text as `nish/json-value` reads a number (`numberText`,
`isI64`, `i64`, `isU64`, `u64`, `f64`), through a tokenizer of its own, so
the two answer alike; the two are separate types until the typed layer
can name a `JsonValue`'s number directly.

A new one holds `0`. Decoding into one reuses its bytes, so an object
decoded again with numbers no longer than before allocates nothing for
them.

```ts
class JsonNumber
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JsonNumber()` |  |
| `bytes: u8[]` | The text is `bytes[0, count)`, one JSON number; the bytes past it are room. |
| `count: i32` |  |
| `f64(): f64` | The nearest `f64`, ties to even, as `JSON.parse` reads it. |
| `i64(): i64` | The value as an `i64` when `isI64()` holds, and `0` otherwise. |
| `isI64(): boolean` | Whether the number is written without a fraction or an exponent and its value fits an `i64`. |
| `isU64(): boolean` | Whether the number is written in digits alone, with no sign, fraction or exponent, and fits a `u64`. |
| `reader(): JsonTokenizer` | A tokenizer over the text, read to its one token. It may open no container and take a number of any length, so it allocates no stack. |
| `setText(text: string): boolean` | Sets the text to `text` when it is one JSON number and nothing else, and answers whether it was; any other text leaves the number as it was. |
| `text(): string` | The number's text, exactly as it was written or set. |
| `u64(): u64` | The value as a `u64` when `isU64()` holds, and `0` otherwise. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="-23" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_DUPLICATE: i32`

A key that names a field the object already gave.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-25" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_MAP_LIMIT: i32`

More keys, over every `Map` field one decoding fills, than `maxMapKeys`;
`errorAt` is the first key past the limit. The global `Map` hashes a
string with no seed, so a body can choose keys that all collide, and the
limit bounds what the maps' probes cost over the whole decoding
(docs/security/json.md, JSON-13).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-24" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_MISSING: i32`

An object that ended without one of the class's fields; `errorAt` is its closing brace.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_OK: i32`

Nothing has failed.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-21" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_RANGE: i32`

A number its field cannot hold: a fraction or an exponent for an integer field, or a value outside its range.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-20" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_TYPE: i32`

A value of the wrong JSON type for its field: a string for an `i32`, an array for a class, `null` for a field that is not `| null`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DECODE_UNKNOWN: i32`

A key that names no field of the class, while `ignoreUnknown` is off.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
